key_insight: A hybrid translator combines deterministic compilation with LLM agents to convert quantum MLIR dialects into QIR, using dual-backend testing to check behavioral agreement.
engineering_relevance: This approach could reduce hand-written compiler work when connecting quantum frameworks to QIR runtimes, while retaining deterministic translation for known dialects.
method: Use deterministic translation for Catalyst and Quake, with an LLM path for unseen dialects and repair after failed tests.
Execute source MLIR and generated QIR on independent simulators; compare output distributions using total variation distance (TVD).
Support smaller open-weight models with inline context and a guardrail assembler that reconstructs valid QIR from incomplete output.
evidence_signal: Across 41 circuits spanning three dialects and 1–100 qubits, deterministic translation was gate-exact on all 70 circuit–dialect pairs with average similarity above 95% (1−TVD); four of six models produced valid logical-level QIR for unseen FTQC on the first iteration.
watch_item: Valid QIR and high distributional similarity do not establish full semantic equivalence or reliable generalization beyond the tested circuits and dialects.
paper_title: Agentic MLIR-to-QIR Translation with Dual-Backend Testing: A Hybrid Deterministic and LLM Approach
